articles.title: 20 years later, veteran WoW director says players outsmarted him completely in Ahn'Qiraj: 'All that work, and there was still an instant tell'
articles.summary: I don't envy the position of being a game developer—especially not an encounter designer in something as complicated as an MMO. You might have an idea of how a mechanic's gonna go, but there's just absolutely no way it survives contact with 40 motivated, mid-2000s era hardcore WoW players.
body: Former game director at Blizzard Wyatt Cheng, whose delightful TikTok channel has been giving free wisdom and anecdotes for some time now, says that exact agony happened to him around 20 years ago with the release of Ahn'Qiraj. Particularly with The Prophet Skeram boss, which splits into illusions at 75%, 50%, and 25% health.

"There's one part I never got right," says Cheng. "I really wanted the only way to tell the difference between the real Skeram and the copies to be that the copies have half the health. So under even DPS rates, the illusions would drop in health faster."

"I pictured raids spreading their DPS and calling it out on [Ventrilo]: Which two are going down quicker?" The idea being, if you didn't kill the illusions first, you'd knock the main Skeram over into his next health threshold and take on additional copies before you're ready: "Now there are five Skerams, and you wipe."

Alas, "that is not how it went. There were so many easy ways to spot the real Skeram. My first version literally had 'Pet of Skeram' written under the copies' names. Oops! In testing, we found more, like UI mods reading creature IDs, or mismatched localisation strings."
points: You might have an idea of how a mechanic's gonna go, but there's just absolutely no way it survives contact with 40 motivated, mid-2000s era hardcore WoW players.

articles.title: Blood of Dawnwalker devs Rebel Wolves are already looking for someone to help write a sequel, so here's where I'd like to see its vampy tale go next
articles.summary: Look, I know it's way to early to be talking about sequels to The Blood of Dawnwalker, given Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG hasn't even been out a week as I write this. However, the game's devs are already putting pieces in place to get on with making such a game, so with help from strong spoiler tags…
body: THIS IS A VERY STRONG SPOILER WARNING FOR THE BLOOD OF DAWNWALKER, YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.

First of all, the sign that Rebel Wolves are wasting no time in cracking on with work to set up their next Dawnwalker entry. "We're not resting on our laurels - no, siree," studio narrative director Jakub Szamalek wrote in a LinkedIn post - that being the natural place for announcements related to sucking the life out of people. "We're already thinking about comes next.

"And so! Drum roll please! I'm looking for a lead writer to help me and the narrative team craft the next chapter in the Dawnwalker saga. We're looking for someone who, to put it bluntly, writes EXCEPTIONALLY well, has a track record of excellence and experience in team management." They're looking for someone with a minimum of six years writing and/or narrative designing in the games industry and "a track record of outstanding achievement".

That's not me, but as someone who writes PASSABLY well and has recently played through the first entry in the series for my Blood of Dawnwalker review, here are a few ideas of what I think would be cool to see from future Dawnwalkings.

articles.title: 'Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys': Meltgate be damned, modders discover RTX 5090 can use 8-pin connectors after all
articles.summary: Ah yes, melty cables. We've been dealing with them ever since the RTX 4090 pushed the 16-pin 12VHPWR connector (now the 12V-2x6 connector) to its limits. Since then, we've heard of numerous cases of melting GPU connectors—check out Uniko's Hardware on X for many examples—and plenty of attempts at…
body: Now, some modders have said 'screw it' to the new 12V-2x6 design, instead modding an RTX 5090 to run on standard 8-pin connectors (via Wccftech ). The modders at TecLab fitted three 8-pin connectors to the back of the PCB using "copper plates, cut by hand", and hooked these up to the front via 24 cables (3x sets of 8).

Once everything was also unlocked to operate at higher power levels, the graphics card was put to the test. And while this was just one batch of tests with one card (and don't try this at home, folks) the results were fantastic.

Even before pushing it as far as it eventually goes, the modders were thrilled with the results (machine translated): "It's getting warmer. It's still colder than a 12VHPWR connector. It's colder than the original connector, guys. Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys. Put the raw footage out there for people to see, otherwise they'll think it's a lie. This looks like a lie."
Don't worry, TecLab, we've got you. You can see the full footage below.

articles.title: Turns out, a lot of Sega's biggest fans don't play its videogames: 'In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play'
articles.summary: There once was a time in which, if you were a fan of a videogame, you might get asked which of said games in the series you had played. Now, I'm not saying we need to bring this era back—it was an obnoxious period full of gatekeepers—but Sega president and COO Shuji Utsumi's recent words on the…
body: Speaking to Nikkei Gaming (thanks, IGN ), Utsumi explains that (via machine translation): "For example, the 'Yakuza' series has been doing exceptionally well in merchandising, with 60-70% of its buyers being women. They've become fans of the 'Yakuza' world, story, and characters after watching our YouTube channel and popular YouTubers' streams. And among them are many people who have never actually played the game."

I'm assuming that Utsumi has stats to back that up, rather than just assuming that women don't play videogames (they do, I work with several of them), but it's indeed true that videogames have been enjoying a wider secondary audience thanks to let's players and streamers.

"Even people who have never played games are considered fans and 'gamers' by us," he adds, "transmedia's strength lies in increasing the entry points and contact points for people to become interested in IP. In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play the games."

articles.title: Rally Point: Strong simulation and team building can't carry Menace forever
articles.summary: It's probably poor form to do another "what I said in a group chat" (this time, to culture critic Rowan Kaiser. Hermits can namedrop too, shut up) intro, but "Oh i already liked menace, that's why I hate it" feels too useful to spurn. I don't really hate Menace.
body: I don't really hate Menace. You've been there, though: a game you enjoy, perhaps even begin to love, but it keeps aggravating you, forcing you to vent before you can play it more. This one is carried through that by a core of turn-based shooting, with some interesting simulation and character levelling that often work well together. And some of its annoyances are natural update fodder during its early access period, as perhaps are some areas that currently feel lacking. But man, does it need that carrying sometimes.

I won't spoil what they are, but it's one of the two or three things you guessed it might be. Although which you guessed might as well be random, as there's no build up to their arrival at all, beyond a very obvious trap. It comes surprisingly far into a game, which I like, but only then are you suddenly expected to know and care who these unskippable and annoying NPCs are, which I obviously don't.

articles.title: That's just great: Graphics card prices in China are set to increase again as Nvidia shifts even more of production towards AI GPUs
articles.summary: In news that will surprise very few, manufacturers are reportedly planning to raise their GPU prices in China again later this month. This could have a knock-on effect on global pricing for both Nvidia and AMD cards.
body: Asus looks set to raise the price of its RTX 5070 cards by between 150 and 300 RMB (roughly between $22 and $45) in mainland China, according to Taiwanese outlet United Daily News. Gigabyte has reportedly already raised the price of its RTX 5060 Ti 16GB GPU by 200 RMB ($30).

AMD has increased prices for a number of cards as well; the RX 9070 XT is up by 200 RMB, the price for both 16G and 8G versions of the RX 9060 XT has increased by up to 250 RMB, and the RX 7650 GRE is up by 400 RMB (about $60). This follows reports in July that AMD would be raising the price of its GPU and VRAM partner bundles by 10%.

Your nemesis and mine, the memory supply crisis, is in part to blame. Nvidia has also been reducing its gaming GPU production for some time now, most recently trimming its shipping forecast by between 15% and 20%.

It would be reasonable to assume the company is shifting production capacity to manufacturing even more AI GPUs. For on thing, Nvidia's data centre segment made $89 billion last quarter alone. Nvidia also just announced it plans to acquire AI development platform Hugging Face for an eye-watering $13 billion.

This could have a knock-on effect on global pricing for both Nvidia and AMD cards.

articles.title: Zombiepunk action RPG Stupid Never Dies is a vibrant feast for the eyes, ears, hands and teeth, even if it is a smidge overwhelming
articles.summary: It's hard to know where to start when talking about Stupid Never Dies. An action RPG built on style, excess and punk ideology. I mean, within the first minutes of my demo starting, I am flushing undead protagonist Davy down a toilet in an abandoned shopping mall to arrive in a hellish arena.
body: Davy, one of very few survivors (can you call a zombie a survivor?) of a worldwide apocalypse, makes his way through and further down into the underworld, all in the hope of reviving his crush Julia — a gorgeous girl who happens to already be frozen to death. Whatever keeps your body warm, Davy. The absurdity continues into the visuals which are based in loud and brash punk stylings, delicately toeing the line of ‘aggressively colourful and busy' and ‘a clusterfuck', and I think it manages to stay on the former side for most of my playtime.

In my time with Stupid Never Dies, I find that even with my power increasing, I still have to concentrate and pay attention to the enemies around me to avoid Davy being buried all over again. A few wrong moves, a few missed Stupid Parries, and he's down. But, if you can keep a cool head, Davy turns into a force of pure momentum, biting cores one after another, parrying directly into enemy attacks rather than trying to dodge and in some cases, activating ‘Davy Burst', a super mode that powers up pretty much every aspect of his moveset and turns him into even more of a monster.

articles.title: I'm not saying Fallout 4 modding drama gets to people, but here's Breaking Benjamin's singer begging concertgoers to try his AI-assisted first person mod
articles.summary: In my experience, the few minutes a live band take between songs to recover a bit before plunging into the next riff are generally quite uneventful. At the most, you might get an amusing story about what they've been up to in your city prior to getting on stage, chatter about the song they're about…
body: "I am an amateur modder," the band's frontman Benjamin Burnley revealed during a mid-gig pause filmed by a Reddit user with the fitting handle im_all_ears. "I make mods for Skyrim and Fallout 4...I just made a mod, it's an F4SE plugin, DLL native plugin, that makes it so that when you're in first person, you stay in first person. You see your body in first person, you go into a workshop in first person." Ok, so far, so slightly unexpected but perfectly normal admission.

First of all, it's obviously not very nice when people are mean to each other on the internet. Second of all, oh mate. If the modder Burnley beefed with was trolling him, odds are they're loving that their efforts have seemingly led to rants across multiple gigs from a celebrity they've clearly succeeded in cheesing off. Burnley even got one of the gig's crew to put the name of his mod, True First Person, up on the big screen, before continuing to promote it by revealing that he was planning on pushing an update for it live. Just over three minutes into the clip, a member of the audience shouts "Play some music!"

articles.title: Blizzard union workers ratify historic contract covering 1,900 employees
articles.summary: Union members have secured guardrails around generative AI usage, layoff protections, remote and hybrid work benefits, and more.
body: Employees at World of Warcraft and Overwatch developer Blizzard have ratified a historic union contract that includes guardrails around AI usage, layoff protections, and remote and hybrid work benefits.
Union members represented by the Communications Workers of America (CWA) claimed the new contract—which covers 1,900 employees across the Microsoft subsidiary—sets a new industry standard.

The union contract delivers wage increases, a three-day hybrid work week, remote working and disability accommodations, and grievance procedures. It also requires Microsoft to discuss, evaluate, and bargain over the usage of artificial intelligence in the workplace.

Notably, in an industry first, it also gives laid off workers the right to be "recalled" into open positions across any Blizzard bargaining unit within 14 months after their layoff was announced. An extra four weeks of severance for union workers has also been secured, irrespective of their tenure at the U.S. company.
points: Union members have secured guardrails around generative AI usage, layoff protections, remote and hybrid work benefits, and more.

body: As a reminder, we have another Direct presentation later today, with Nintendo promising a look at games launching during the Winter – along with a few surprises for the more distant future, no doubt.

But as for the Zelda Direct, we've slept on it and had some time to digest what we've seen from Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, so now it's time for Team NL to provide their thoughts on what Nintendo showcased.

Glimpsing the game on a phone screen while jogging to a departure gate was a suboptimal way to get a first (proper) look at it, and, as pretty as it is, I absolutely get the 'Unreal Engine mod' takes. The granular details on the leather braided belts and Epona's hair are impressive, but everything looks exceptionally shiny. Link and Saria's faces felt off initially — the former too angular and the latter too soft — and Saria's voice sounded gratingly cutesy.

articles.title: Persona 4 Revival Is Officially Heading To Switch 2, With Persona 6 Teased For The Future
articles.summary: Bit Persona-l. After being announced for just about every other system, we had our fingers crossed that Persona 4 Revival might be making its way to Switch 2 too, and what do you know, it is! This one will come our way on 20th May 2027 — a few months later than the PS5 release, but what can you do?
body: For those unfamiliar with the base game, we've included an official bit of blurb below. But rest assured, this looks to be your full-fat Persona experience, complete with school drama, cracking tunes, and just a bit of murder.

In Persona 4 Revival, legend has it that a mysterious broadcast known as the "Midnight Channel" appears only on rainy nights. The day after it airs, a corpse is found in Inaba, a quiet and peaceful town in rural Japan suddenly thrown into turmoil. To uncover the truth behind these chilling mysteries, you and your friends form an investigation team to unravel the secrets of the Midnight Channel and the bizarre murders. As your adventure unfolds, you face off against "Shadows," eerie manifestations of individuals' darker selves. Together, you awaken a hidden power called "Persona" and embark on a journey to prevent more tragedies while uncovering the truth behind the chaos.
But that's not all from Atlus, as the studio followed the Revival announcement with a Persona 6 tease, confirming that it'll also be coming to Switch 2!

articles.title: Everything We Saw At The September Nintendo Direct
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda had its moment, but there are plenty other games coming to Switch 2
body: Nintendo has held two Direct showcases this week. Yesterday’s was all about the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda, and today’s was a more general presentation about games coming to Switch 2. If you want to watch the show but couldn’t catch it live, you can watch the VOD below. If you just want to scroll through the highlights, read on.

Kicking things off is a new look at Monster Hunter Wilds, which is finally coming to Switch 2 with all its previous updates and local co-op support on December 4. It’ll be followed by the Ascendance expansion coming out next year.

Because we haven’t seen enough of it between Gamescom and the State of Play, we got another brief look at Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which is coming to the Switch 2 (and everything else) on April 8. Also, Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII Reunion is shadow dropping on Switch 2 today.

The Zelda musou game Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity is coming to the Switch 2 with all its expansion pass content and a new Calamity Mode difficulty setting. Those who bought the game on Switch 1 will get a discount when upgrading to the Switch 2 version. It launches on February 25.
points: The Legend of Zelda had its moment, but there are plenty other games coming to Switch 2
